question: May plugins author canonical AI-safety attestations, and if so must plugin identity, origin, trust, and allowed event types be derived entirely by the host loader?
rationale: The answer defines a permanent public plugin contract and the trust meaning of safety telemetry, which cannot be resolved safely from implementation mechanics alone.

options.title: Host-owned canonical events
options.body: Keep canonical AI-safety attestations host-owned and expose plugin-originated observations as separately identified plugin diagnostics.

options.title: Bound plugin emission
options.body: Allow plugin-authored safety events only through a loader-injected emitter whose identity, origin, and manifest declarations are host-derived.

options.title: Caller-selected facade
options.body: Approve the raw facade and explicitly document that its trust metadata is advisory rather than a security boundary.

recommendation.title: Host-owned canonical events
recommendation.body: Keep canonical AI-safety attestations host-owned and expose plugin-originated observations as separately identified plugin diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: This cross-cutting plugin SDK and security-boundary choice needs repository-level product ownership.
